faq.a: Elmas is associated with the Arabic form أَلْمَاس, whose core sense is elmas; diamond (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Elmas?
faq.a: Elmas is associated with Arabic. Elmas is the Turkish form of Arabic أَلْمَاس (Almās), meaning 'diamond'.
Yes — the underlying form أَلْمَاس is Arabic.
Elmas can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Elmas should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Almās is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Elmas, elmas. Script forms are أَلْمَاس, الماس, एल्मास.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
